title: Presentability of the infinity category of nonsymmetric infinity operads
statement: Fix universes and the infinity-category conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], and let $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}_{\mathrm{inert}}$ be the subcategory of $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ consisting of inert maps (those corresponding to inclusions of consecutive subintervals). Let $\operatorname{Opd}^{\mathrm{ns}}_\infty$ be the infinity category whose objects are small inner fibrations $\pi:\mathcal O^\otimes\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ such that every inert map admits a $\pi$-cocartesian lift and the inert Segal maps $\mathcal O_{[n]}\to\mathcal O_{[1]}^n$ are equivalences, with the following relative-limit condition: for every $C\in\mathcal O_{[n]}$, its chosen cocartesian inert projections $C\to C_i$ over $\rho_i:[n]\to[1]$, every $X\in\mathcal O_{[m]}$ and every $\phi:[m]\to[n]$, composition gives an equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal O}^{\phi}(X,C)\simeq\prod_{i=1}^n\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal O}^{\rho_i\phi}(X,C_i)$. Here $\operatorname{Map}^{\phi}$ is the homotopy fiber of the map on mapping spaces over the base arrow $\phi$; the empty product for $n=0$ is a point. An inert operad edge means a cocartesian edge over an inert base map. The morphisms of $\operatorname{Opd}^{\mathrm{ns}}_\infty$ are functors over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ carrying inert cocartesian edges to inert cocartesian edges. Use presentability as in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. In the fixed universe, $\operatorname{Opd}^{\mathrm{ns}}_\infty$ is a presentable infinity category: it is accessible and admits colimits of every small simplicial diagram.

source.place: Section 3.2, opening paragraph; Definitions 3.2.1-3.2.3, Example 3.2.4(i), Corollary 3.2.6 and Definition 3.2.7, printed pp.606-608. All operads are small in the fixed smaller universe. Shared archive WANTED; source digest in report.md.

proof.text: Put $B=N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ and let $S$ be its inert edges; $S$ contains the degenerate edges. For each $n\geq0$ let $K_n$ be the discrete category with objects $1,\ldots,n$ and take the cone $p_n:K_n^{\triangleleft}\to B$ with apex $[n]$, other vertices $[1]$, and edges $\rho_i$. For $n=0$ it is just the vertex $[0]$, an empty $K_0$, which [def-coef-categorical-pattern-fibrancy] allows. These are small quasicategories and form a small family; identities and every $\rho_i$ lie in $S$. Thus $\mathfrak P=(B,S,\{p_n\})$ is a categorical pattern in the sense of [def-coef-categorical-pattern-fibrancy], with all $2$-simplices scaled. Let $\mathcal M$ be the left proper combinatorial simplicial model structure on $\mathsf M_{\mathfrak P}$ given by [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus]. Its cofibrations are the maps injective on simplices, so all its objects are cofibrant.

By [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus] the fibrant objects of $\mathcal M$ are exactly the $\mathfrak P$-fibered objects of [def-coef-categorical-pattern-fibrancy]; unpack its conditions for these discrete $K_n$. Condition (i) is the specified inner fibration, and (ii) gives exactly the inert cocartesian lifts and says that the marking is exactly the inert cocartesian edges. The classifying functor in (iii) has values $\mathcal O_{[n]}$ at its apex and $\mathcal O_{[1]}$ at each other vertex, and arrows given by inert transport, by [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]. A limit over $n$ discrete vertices is their product; the finite products in $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ are the stated products of infinity categories. Hence (iii) is precisely $\mathcal O_{[n]}\simeq\mathcal O_{[1]}^n$. A cocartesian section over $K_n^{\triangleleft}$ is an object $C\in\mathcal O_{[n]}$ with cocartesian edges $C\to C_i$ over $\rho_i$, and any two such choices are equivalent. Condition (iv) asks that, for $X\in\mathcal O_{[m]}$, the square with top $\operatorname{Map}(X,C)\to\prod_i\operatorname{Map}(X,C_i)$ and bottom $\operatorname{Map}([m],[n])\to\prod_i\operatorname{Map}([m],[1])$ be a homotopy pullback. A square of spaces is a homotopy pullback exactly when the induced map of homotopy fibers of its vertical maps over every base point of the lower left corner is an equivalence; over $\phi:[m]\to[n]$ the left fiber is $\operatorname{Map}^{\phi}(X,C)$ and, since homotopy fibers commute with products, the right fiber over $(\rho_i\phi)_i$ is $\prod_i\operatorname{Map}^{\rho_i\phi}(X,C_i)$. So (iv) is exactly the product comparison of mapping fibers in the item (the formulation of Remark 3.1.4). These identifications work in both directions. For $n=0$, (iii) gives a terminal $\mathcal O_{[0]}$ and (iv) gives the mapping fiber equivalent to the empty product point. Consequently the fibrant objects of $\mathcal M$ are exactly the specified operads with all and only inert cocartesian edges marked.

Use the simplicial category of fibrant objects of $\mathcal M$ to model $\operatorname{Opd}^{\mathrm{ns}}_\infty$, as in Definition 3.2.7. This identifies the intended coherent infinity category, including its morphisms: a marked map over $B$ preserves precisely inert operad edges, while an $r$-simplex in the enriched Hom is a coherent family parameterized by $(\Delta^r)^\sharp$, namely a marked map $(\mathcal O,T)\times(\Delta^r)^\sharp\to(\mathcal P,U)$ over $B$, the $r$-simplices of $\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_B$ in [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus], whose composition is composition of these families. On each source vertex a parameter arrow is cocartesian over an identity. To check that it is an equivalence, apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]: precomposition with this arrow $e:x\to y$ is an equivalence on every mapping space because the bottom map of its homotopy pullback square is the identity. For target $x$ choose $r:y\to x$ with $re\simeq1_x$; for target $y$, injectivity on components then gives $er\simeq1_y$ since $(er)e\simeq e$. By [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences], these objectwise equivalences are equivalence edges in the functor infinity category. Conversely, for a coherent family over $B$ whose vertices preserve inert edges and whose parameter edges are objectwise equivalences, the mapping criterion says that each parameter edge over an identity is cocartesian: both horizontal maps of its square are equivalences. A mixed marked edge in $\mathcal O\times\Delta^r$ is the third edge of the triangle obtained by first traversing its source-operad edge at the initial parameter vertex and then its parameter edge at the terminal source vertex. The first image is cocartesian because that vertex functor preserves inert edges; the second is cocartesian by the preceding criterion. Their composite is cocartesian by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality]. Its base arrow is inert, so this mixed edge is marked in the target. This proves the converse marking condition for every simplex; faces and degeneracies are restrictions of the same families. The enriched compositions give their coherent composition. This is the space of inert-preserving functors and their equivalences, with higher coherences, not the discrete set of such functors. Since every object is cofibrant, $\mathcal M^f=\mathcal M^{cf}$, and the coherent nerve of this simplicial category is the intended model of $\operatorname{Opd}^{\mathrm{ns}}_\infty$.

source.place: Definition 3.2.7 (arXiv 1312.3178); explicit interpretation of its simplicial category of fibrant objects

proof.text: Apply the first, nonmonoidal assertion of [lem-coef-combinatorial-localization-presentability] to $\mathcal M$: its required local presentability and set-generated functorial weak factorization systems are supplied by combinatoriality in [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus] (combinatorial as specified in [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model]: locally presentable with both weak factorization systems generated by sets, functorial factorizations being part of its notion of model structure, exactly the hypotheses of the localization node). Its homotopy coherent localization is therefore presentable. By [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], that same localization is modeled by $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathcal M^{cf})$, which step 3 identifies with $\operatorname{Opd}^{\mathrm{ns}}_\infty$. Presentability of this infinity category means precisely accessibility and existence of every small simplicial colimit by [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. All model-category objects and all indexing diagrams here are small in the fixed smaller universe; the category of them lies in the ambient larger universe.

Maintainer review replaced the delivered duplicate general pattern node by this existing pair.

lean.note: The object notion is the full subcategory of marked over-base objects whose marking is exactly inert cocartesian edges plus degeneracies, with inner fibration, inert lifts, Segal fibers, and the recorded HasMonoidalRelativeLimits triangle-graph comparison. The category is SimplicialNerve of this enriched full subcategory, hence the coherent nerve with Map♯ over the base and higher coherences. The marked-object predicate reuses SSet.Enhanced.IsChainTwoInfinityOperad from the acyclic ComposableBimoduleOperadSegal module; despite its historical name this is the general ordinary nonsymmetric operad predicate. The existential quasicategory proof is redundant for an inner fibration over the simplex nerve, so no hypothesis is added. The canonical enrichment is specified up to enriched isomorphism by its mapping, ordinary-map and composition normalizations.
